prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation by induced proximity, from PROTACs to the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide-type molecular glues

statement.case_for: I keep targeted protein degradation (B057) as a single-part prize with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. Round 1 did not weaken the scientific case: all eight members accept that ternary-complex formation, E3 recruitment and cereblon as the thalidomide target are confirmed, and the dispute is about timing and the cut. Induced proximity is a new chemical mode of action, catalytic and event-driven, not occupancy-based, and the ternary-complex energetics (cooperativity, interface complementarity, linker effects) make it a hard chemical problem, which answers the question of whether this is chemistry. The trio spans concept and mechanism: Crews and Deshaies built and demonstrated PROTACs, and Handa's cereblon identification explains an old pharmacological puzzle and anchors the glue arm, which is the part with approved drugs behind it. On the chair's questions, I am prepared to award before a degrader is approved, because the thalidomide-class drugs already show the mechanism acting in patients and the credit picture will not change by waiting. I prefer one citation covering both arms, since the shared principle is induced proximity, and I do not support a two-part split that a three-name cap cannot fill fairly.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC drug is approved, so the field could be judged a few years early, and the clinical argument rests on trial momentum. The cut is real: Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structure), Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim have serious claims, and the PROTAC and glue strands have different histories, so one citation may read as two achievements joined. Brzezinski's point that Ciulli is the chemically most interesting contributor is one I cannot dismiss. Finally, B037 (Car-Parrinello), which I ranked first in the opening, remains the most mature and cleanly attributed candidate, but it has no support beyond me and I do not present it as a committee preference.

responses.point: Brzezinski keeps B054 as his preferred prize and still argues for Ciulli over Handa or Deshaies as third name, with B057 possibly early.
responses.response: I considered Ciulli again, as he was in my own opening trio. Replacing Handa with Ciulli would narrow the citation to PROTACs and leave molecular glues, the part of the field with approved drugs, without a founder. Replacing Deshaies would drop one of the two people who conceived and first demonstrated PROTACs in cells. Neither trade seems better, so I keep Crews, Deshaies and Handa. I agree with you that B054 is mature and clean, and I would accept it as the fallback if B057 is judged premature, but I do not think timing alone should displace a new mode of action.

responses.point: Somfai prefers B068 (Buchwald and Hartwig) as the cleanest case on maturity and attribution, with B057 as first alternative.
responses.response: I accept that B068 is the cleanest case on the shortlist for maturity and for two-person attribution, and I do not question the science. My remaining hesitation is the 2010 cross-coupling prize and Kosugi's precursor, which would need explicit citation wording about catalytic, ligand-controlled C-N coupling. Zou's point that C-N coupling needed new ligand design and mechanism is fair, but I still judge that a new mode of chemical action carries more weight than an extension of a recognised class. If B057 fails to reach five votes I would take B068 seriously as a fallback alongside B054.

responses.point: Zou argues that the 2010 prize covered C-C coupling and not C-N coupling, and says she would support B057 if the clinical evidence is sufficient.
responses.response: Your distinction between C-C and C-N bond formation is a reasonable one and eases my 2010 reservation about B068. On your conditional support for B057, I would say that the evidence the committee already has is mechanistic and reproduced across laboratories, and that cereblon-based drugs act in patients today. That seems sufficient to me for a prize on the concept and mechanism, which is what the proposed citation honours, not on an approved PROTAC.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, records that the PROTAC and glue strands may be one or two achievements and that B054 is the safer choice if the blur is unacceptable.
responses.response: I treat them as one achievement because both arms use a small molecule to bring a target to an E3 ligase, and Handa's cereblon work shows that glues act through the same logic as PROTACs. I would accept B054 as the fallback you describe, and I note that Brzezinski's point about distinctness from the 2018 directed-evolution prize would need careful wording. I retract my earlier remark favouring a B016 and B054 comparison, since neither seems more urgent than settling B057.

responses.point: Aili would accept B037 as a better-defined option if a three-person split for B057 cannot be agreed.
responses.response: I appreciate the support for B037, but I do not want to push it. Only I ranked it, and a prize that cannot reach five votes is not a real fallback. The three-person split for B057 is, in my view, settled enough: the identical Crews, Deshaies, Handa trio appears in the round-1 preferences of five members, so I do not think the committee needs to fall back to B037 this year.

uncertainties: Whether five members will accept a degradation prize before any degrader is approved.
Whether Handa is a better third name than Ciulli once the citation covers both PROTACs and glues, and whether Ito is under-credited by this choice.
Whether B054 or B068 is the right fallback if B057 falls short, given the recent biomolecular-tool prizes.
statement.conflict_note: No change. My documented tie to Arieh Warshel (postdoctoral EVB collaboration) concerns no shortlisted candidate, and none of the credited names is linked to Uppsala University or to my own work. No recusal is requested.
